Hawkwood is a remarkable portrait of one of the late fourteenth century’s most colourful characters, John Hawkwood – an Essex boy who became the greatest mercenary in an age when soldiers of fortune flourished.
‘This was the age of the new man, and John Hawkwood was the most audacious of them all. His scheme, quite simply, was to hold Europe’s richest country to ransom, and he turned the business of war into an exorbitant art.

It was said of Hawkwood that ‘an Englishman Italianised is a devil incarnate’, and Frances Stonor Saunders sheds light on this dark legend.
